selected.reason: Allowlist of approved documentation hosts/APIs prevents the model from choosing arbitrary destinations.
Granular fetch tool avoids open-ended URL fetching functionality.
Internal API credential must be securely stored server-side, never exposed to the model.
Avoid open-ended shell execution; restrict to allowlisted, granular test commands.
Model-selected input must never be passed directly to dynamic command execution.
Resource quotas (CPU, memory, time) must bound tool execution.
Sandboxing the test execution enforces filesystem boundary controls.
Token issuer/key material must come from trusted pre-configured sources, not token-supplied JWK URLs.
Tenant ownership checks must rely on trusted server-side data, not client-supplied claims.
Project access must be restricted to tenants with explicit permission to prevent BOLA.
Centralized authorization check for tenant/project ownership improves consistency.
State, nonce, and PKCE code_verifier must be bound to the initiating session per this control.
New session must be established after successful authentication to prevent fixation.
CSRF-style random tokens reinforce protection against forged callback requests.
Model must be verified via signing/hash checks from a verifiable source before bundling.
Verify integrity of downloaded model files via checksums/cryptographic hashes before use.
Ensures pinned version comes from the expected approved source, avoiding substitution attacks.
Prevents dependency confusion by ensuring package resolves from the expected private registry.
SBOM/inventory helps verify component provenance and trusted sources.
Provenance data must be collected and preserved for release artifacts.
Service account running the tunnel must operate with least privilege.
Service accounts used for external connections should have minimal privileges.
Strong authentication (host-key verification) required for inter-service SSH connections.
Keep autossh and system packages patched to reduce known vulnerabilities.

coverageGaps.reason: Catalog lacks a specific control for strict SSH host-key verification workflows.

selected.reason: API token must be stored in a secrets management solution, not in the unit file or repo.
Credentials must be encrypted/stored securely and never hardcoded.
Backup uploads over HTTPS require TLS for sensitive data in transit.
Dedicated unprivileged account should follow least privilege.

coverageGaps.control: Fail-safe local retention on remote failure
coverageGaps.reason: No catalog policy addresses preserving local backups on upload failure.

selected.reason: Uploaded JSON fields are untrusted and must be validated before processing.
Malformed or invalid policy documents must be rejected outright.
Tool-permission enforcement must occur in deterministic code, not be delegated to claims within the imported document.
Oversized documents should be rejected via length/size validation.
File names/paths from archive entries must be validated to prevent path traversal (zip-slip).
File-count and expanded-size limits directly enforce input length/size validation to prevent resource exhaustion (zip bombs).
Sandboxing the inspection process limits impact of malicious archive content.
Direct object reference (invoice ID) must be restricted to the owning account to prevent IDOR.
Support staff access must go through the centralized authorization service.
Authorization decisions must rely on trusted server-side account/user identifiers, not client input.
Explicit object-level access control mitigates BOLA/IDOR.
User-submitted URLs are untrusted and must be strictly validated before use.
Allowlist of permitted external destinations is essential to prevent SSRF to internal/private endpoints.
Redirects followed by the HTTP client must also be validated to prevent SSRF bypass.

coverageGaps.reason: Catalog has no dedicated SSRF/DNS-rebinding control for blocking loopback/link-local ranges.
